entries.subject: Radius, mass and orbit adopted from the published record
entries.finding: Radius 0.7538 Jupiter radii, mass 0.333 Jupiter masses, a2 = 0.7048 au, i2 = 90.0322 degrees, e2 = 0.0069, omega2 = 318 degrees and the mean longitude 106.51 degrees at BJD 2455212.12316 from Doyle et al. (2011), Table 1. The orbit is about the barycentre of A and B.

entries.subject: Which period carries the planet to the scene epoch
entries.finding: Doyle et al.'s osculating 228.776 d misplaces the seven Kepler transits by -2.6 to +18.7 d. Triaud et al. (2022)'s mean 226.0 +/- 1.7 d has a phase uncertain by 92 d. The Villanova catalogue's mean transit period 225.885 d with Doyle's mean longitude puts all seven transits within 0.13 d.

entries.subject: The precessing orbit and the end of transits
entries.finding: Doyle et al. predict transits across A to cease in early 2018 and return around 2042, and those across B to stop for 35 years from May 2014. A fixed ellipse keeps the 2010 tilt; showing the precession would need the three-body model at the scene epoch.

entries.subject: Any image, colour or spectrum of the planet
entries.finding: None published: the planet is known from transits, eclipse timing and radial velocities only.
